_comment: Buyer-readable expected outputs for the demo. The machine-checked version of this file is evals/gold_queries.json; q1 is graded by its synthesis citations (multi-document trace), not keywords.

q1.expected_shape: An evidence-cited synthesis concluding the Fleet Pro increase is margin-driven but competitively vulnerable: price rose while offline mode was removed, Atlas undercuts it at $59 and keeps the capability that 4 in 10 Fleet Pro customers call important or critical, and Aurora's estimated 55% margin suggests it can hold its price. Every claim must cite edge ids that trace to at least four of the six documents.

q2.expected_answer: Atlas is priced at $59 per month per site.

q3.expected_answer: Insufficient evidence — the corpus never states headcount, so the kit must refuse rather than answer from model memory.

q4.expected_answer: Fleet Pro rose from $49 to $79/month effective July 1, 2026, driven (per the CFO) by cloud infrastructure costs pressuring margins; the new price is $20/month above Aurora's competing Atlas at $59/month per site.
